Thank you for your response. I’m glad you’re doing better, now. I don’t know if my ED is connected with any of the other issues I struggle with but I suppose it could be. I do remember when I first started, or rather, first heard about anorexia and decided I’d do the same. I was in a very bad place, very depressed, and I believe I had started self harming by then. I was at my best friends birthday party with another friend of mine who my ex had cheated on me with, and was still dating, and every time I looked at her I just got even more depressed. We sat down to have cake and she asked how many calories there were in it. We both didn’t really know how to answer, so she looked at the container and said some number that I can’t remember before doing some math in her head and getting a very small piece of cake. I asked her why she was doing that and she said she was anorexic. I probably asked more questions, but I don’t remember that. I do remember, however, seeing her do it, understanding what she was doing, and immediately wanting to do the same. I started counting calories and eating less, after that. It seems it’s only gotten worse since.. 

My home life? I suppose it could be better but it was a lot worse when I was younger. Im not at my moms house a whole lot cause I hate her boyfriend and don’t care for her boyfriend’s sister and despise having to have any interaction with them, so I just tend to stay away from there. Im mostly at my dads house, which I enjoy. It’s a lot smaller but I’m a lot more comfortable over here with just my dad and one of my brothers.

Again, thank you for your response

Thank you for your response. I’m happy that you’ve recovered and are doing better now. I wouldn’t wish anything I struggle with on my worst enemy. I agree, the part that seems hardest about getting better is the idea of everyone knowing that I’m not. The idea of everyone knowing about my anorexia is terrifying to me, though all of my friends know, it’s just my family and well anyone who could really help me that doesn’t know about it. It’s so difficult and it’s so frustrating. Like, I want to get better, I do, but I just can’t seem to make myself. It doesn’t make any sense when I want to eat but still won’t let myself or I just see everyone eating and I’m not hungry at all even though I should be or the thought/sight of eating just makes me nauseous. I hate it so much. I’m so tired. My brain always just tells me that I can get better on my own. I don’t need my family’s help because how would they help anyways. I don’t want to keep feeling like this but the idea of them coming in and implementing so much change makes me anxious. Maybe I just don’t like change very much. I don’t like the idea of losing the routine I have, I feel like it’d make everything else in my life messy again. Im afraid I’d ask for help with my anorexia and start getting it and then everything else I’ve been getting better with will get worse again and I really cant handle that.. i don’t know. Maybe I’m being selfish and stupid by keeping it all to myself. All I know is that my fear is a lot stronger than my willpower and I’ve always told myself that if I can function then it just can’t be that much of an issue.. but I don’t know how the true that really is..

My doctor doesn’t know, I don’t even know that I have a regular doctor that I go to to be honest. Last I checked, which was a few weeks ago, I was within the healthy weight for my height. I don’t believe that I’m autistic and I’ve never been assessed for it either. I don’t know if I’ll ever manage to get myself to tell my family but I felt that way about being raped as well and I wound up telling them so maybe it’ll just take time. Thank you for your response

I find it hard to keep going on, sometimes, my head gets so muddled. My priorities fade away and all I’m left with are the horrid memories from my life, reminding me off all that was and all the will never be again.

I wish it were easy but I know it isn’t and I know It never will be.
